questions.prompt: Which are the listed infrastructure deployment options?

options.text: On premise
Hosted
Cloud
Floppy disk

questions.explanation: Infrastructure deployment: on premise (own servers), hosted (third-party centers), and cloud (virtualized).

questions.prompt: What is a characteristic of an in-place upgrade?

options.text: Installation on top of the current version, requiring downtime
Two parallel environments with a load balancer
Gradual traffic shift node by node
Zero downtime always guaranteed

questions.explanation: In-place upgrade installs on top of the current version, requires downtime, and preserves existing settings.

questions.prompt: In blue-green deployment, what is the role of the 'green' environment when 'blue' is in production?

options.text: It is idle, used to deploy and test the new version before traffic is switched
It serves all production traffic simultaneously
It is permanently decommissioned
It hosts the database only

questions.explanation: In blue-green, blue runs the current app while green is idle; the new version is deployed and tested on green, then a load balancer switches all traffic to it.

options.text: Only a few nodes get the new version, receiving a minority of requests, then it scales up if healthy
All nodes are upgraded at once
Two complete environments are alternated
The system is taken fully offline

questions.explanation: Canary ('canary in the coal mine'): a few nodes host the new version, the load balancer forwards a minority of requests, and the percentage increases incrementally if no issues.

questions.prompt: With feature flags, canary exposes changes to a small group of users, whereas rolling exposes changes on a small group of nodes.
questions.explanation: Canary with feature flags targets a small group of users; rolling with feature flags is the same but exposure is made on nodes, not users.

questions.prompt: What is the goal of a deployment diagram?

options.text: To map software systems and containers onto deployment nodes
To show class-level inheritance
To define business rules
To list user stories

questions.explanation: A deployment diagram maps software systems and containers (deployable units) onto deployment nodes, using the C4 model with boundaries per node.

questions.prompt: Which can serve as a 'deployment node'?

options.text: Physical infrastructure (e.g. a physical server)
Virtualized infrastructure (e.g. a VM / IaaS)
Containerised infrastructure (e.g. a Docker container)
An execution environment (e.g. a database server)

questions.explanation: A deployment node can be physical infrastructure, virtualized infrastructure, containerised infrastructure, or an execution environment.

questions.prompt: In blue-green deployment, once traffic is switched the former green environment becomes the main one and the blue becomes idle, with alternation continuing on the next release.
questions.explanation: After switching traffic to green, green becomes production and blue goes idle; the two environments alternate roles on each subsequent release.

questions.prompt: What happens in a canary deployment if problems are detected in the new version?

options.text: The load balancer can temporarily reverse/reduce traffic to the new version
All nodes are immediately upgraded anyway
The system must be taken fully offline
The old version is permanently deleted

questions.explanation: If problems arise, the load balancer can temporarily reverse the balance (reduce traffic to the new version) until issues are resolved.

options.text: Hosted means installed on third-party data centers; cloud means virtualized over the cloud
Hosted means virtualized; cloud means on your own servers
They are identical
Hosted requires no servers at all

questions.explanation: On premise = your own servers; hosted = installed on third-party centers; cloud = the system is virtualized over the cloud.

questions.prompt: How do canary deployments with feature flags work?

options.text: New features are flagged in code and enabled via configuration for a small group of users, then progressively expanded
New features are always enabled for everyone at once
Features can only be toggled by redeploying the whole system
Feature flags disable monitoring

questions.explanation: With feature flags, new features are flagged in code and enabled via configuration for a small 'canary' group of users, then progressively expanded (or reduced if problems arise).

questions.prompt: Which method is used to draw a deployment diagram?

options.text: The C4 model with further boundaries for each deployment node
A UML state machine per node
An entity-relationship diagram
A flamegraph

questions.explanation: A deployment diagram uses the C4 model with additional boundaries for each deployment node (physical, virtualized, containerised, or an execution environment).
